directAnswer: Benedict IX's third and final term as pope began after Clement II's death in October 1047 and ended in July 1048, when Margrave Boniface of Tuscany, acting for Emperor Henry III, drove him from Rome. He made no further successful claim to the papacy and died around 1055 or 1056.

sections.h2: Seizing the Opportunity of Clement II's Death
paras: When Clement II died unexpectedly in October 1047, Benedict IX, who had never accepted his removal at Sutri, moved quickly. With the support of his family and allies in Rome, he regained control of the Lateran. The official list dates this third pontificate from 9 October 1047.

Henry III did not accept Benedict's return. He nominated Poppo, bishop of Brixen, as pope and ordered Boniface, margrave of Tuscany, to install him. Boniface at first hesitated, but under the emperor's pressure he marched on Rome, and Benedict was driven out in July 1048. Poppo became Damasus II, though he died within weeks.

Benedict was afterward excommunicated, and he never again held Rome. The details of his last years are thin. A tradition associated with the abbey of Grottaferrata, near Tusculum, holds that he ended his life there in penance, and he probably died around 1055 or 1056. His three reigns remain a unique and cautionary episode in papal history.

keyFacts: Returned to power after the death of Clement II
Expelled by Margrave Boniface of Tuscany on Henry III's orders
Succeeded by Damasus II (Poppo of Brixen)

faqs.question: How did Benedict IX's third pontificate end?
faqs.answer: Emperor Henry III ordered Margrave Boniface of Tuscany to remove him, and Boniface expelled him from Rome in July 1048.

faqs.question: Did Benedict IX repent?
faqs.answer: A tradition linked to the abbey of Grottaferrata holds that he died there as a penitent, but this cannot be confirmed from contemporary sources.
